---
name: policy-security
description: Security policy of the todo app team (version 1). Rules for input handling, destructive operations, rendering user text and dependencies. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or code that reads files or input, deletes or overwrites data, renders user text, or adds a dependency.
version: 1
owner: Khoa (tech lead, also security owner, simulated) · backup: Mai (simulated)
---

# Security policy · v1

Sample policy for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-security@1#S<n>`.

- **S1.** Treat every imported file as untrusted. Validate it against the expected schema, reject unknown fields, cap its size at
  1 MB, never evaluate its content.
- **S2.** Any operation that overwrites or deletes more than one item asks for an explicit confirmation **before** it runs, and the
  confirmation says what will be lost (for example "Thay 12 việc hiện có bằng 30 việc trong file?").
- **S3.** Render user-provided text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.
- **S4.** No new external dependency (CDN script, library, web service) without sign-off from the security owner.

13	  next.
14	- **U2.** No confirmation dialogs for actions on a single item: they happen at once and offer **Undo** for 10 seconds instead.
15	  Actions that overwrite or delete more than one item follow `policy-security#S2` (confirm first). *(Changed in v2, agreed by the UX
16	  and security owners, 2026-10-20.)*
17	- **U3.** Every list or screen defines its empty, loading and error states.
18	- **U4.** UI text is Vietnamese, short, and free of technical words (no "localStorage", "JSON", "console").
19	- **U5.** Every control works with the keyboard and has an accessible label.

name: policy-ux
description: UX standard of the todo app team (version 2). Rules for feedback on failures, confirmations, screen states, wording and accessibility. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or UI code for the app.
version: 2
owner: Linh (UX owner, simulated) · backup: Thảo (product owner, simulated)
---

# UX standard · v2

Sample standard for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-ux@2#U<n>`.

- **U1.** Never lose the user's data silently. Any failed save is shown on the same screen, in plain words, with what the user can do
  next.
- **U2.** No confirmation dialogs for actions on a single item: they happen at once and offer **Undo** for 10 seconds instead.
  Actions that overwrite or delete more than one item follow `policy-security#S2` (confirm first). *(Changed in v2, agreed by the UX
  and security owners, 2026-10-20.)*
- **U3.** Every list or screen defines its empty, loading and error states.
- **U4.** UI text is Vietnamese, short, and free of technical words (no "localStorage", "JSON", "console").
- **U5.** Every control works with the keyboard and has an accessible label.

1	---
2	name: policy-privacy
3	description: Privacy policy of the todo app team (version 1). Rules for any change that stores, moves, exports or shows user data. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or code that touches user data, storage, export/import, backup or sync.
4	version: 1
5	owner: Mai (privacy owner, simulated) · backup: Khoa (tech lead, simulated)
6	---
7	
8	# Privacy policy · v1
9	
10	Sample policy for the demo. Not legal advice. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-privacy@1#P<n>`.
11	
12	- **P1.** User data never leaves the user's device without an explicit action by that user. No background upload, no analytics, no
13	  third-party service.
14	- **P2.** Anything exported contains only data the user created. No device identifiers, no browser fingerprint.
15	- **P3.** Exported files are plain and human-readable, so the user can open one and see exactly what is inside.
16	- **P4.** Tell the user, in plain words inside the app, where their data is kept and what happens when they clear it.
17	- **P5.** Storing user data anywhere outside the user's browser (server, cloud, account) needs sign-off from the privacy owner first.
18

Sample policy for the demo. Not legal advice. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-privacy@1#P<n>`.

# Plan: "Xoá việc đã xong" (clear completed)

Status: draft · Size: **Medium** (4 files: `app/index.html`, `app/app.js`, `app/backup.js`, `tests/app.test.js`) ·
Policies applied: `policy-security@1`, `policy-ux@2`, `policy-privacy@1`

## Context
Users finish tasks but can only delete them one by one (`remove(id)`, `app/app.js:19`). They want one button that removes every
finished task. This deletes many items at once, so it falls under **policy-security@1#S2**: confirm *before* it runs, and the
question says what will be lost. The repo's process is intent → spec → plan; there is no intent for this yet (see "Before code").

## Decisions a person must make (not picked by the agent)
| Q | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Exactly **1** finished task: `U2` says single-item actions get no dialog but an **Undo for 10 s**. The app has no Undo today (single `×` delete has none either). | Ask Linh (UX owner). Options: (a) confirm for every n ≥ 1, written down as a U2 exception; (b) build Undo (bigger change, would make this Large-ish). I lean (a). |
| Q2 | Show the button while the saved list is unreadable (`store.readError`)? Nothing is saved then anyway (`save()` → `'skipped'`). | Keep it, same as add/toggle/×: banner already says changes are not saved. |
| Q3 | Wording (U4, Vietnamese, short). | Button `Xoá việc đã xong`; question `Xoá {n} việc đã xong? Không lấy lại được.`; yes-button `Xoá`; result `Đã xoá {n} việc đã xong.` Linh approves. |

## Files that change
- `app/index.html` — `<button type="button" id="clear-done">Xoá việc đã xong</button>` next to `#count`. Confirm dialog's yes
  button gets an id (`#confirm-yes`) so its label can change; it is hard-coded `Thay` today (line 37), wrong for a delete.
- `app/backup.js` — add to `MESSAGES` (all UI text lives there): `confirmClearDone`, `clearedDone`. No new logic file.
- `app/app.js`
  - `ask(question, yes = 'Thay')`: sets `#confirm-yes` text, so import keeps "Thay" and clear uses "Xoá".
  - `async function clearDone()`: `n = todos.filter(t => t.done).length`; if `n === 0` return; `if (!(await ask(fill(MESSAGES.confirmClearDone, { n }), 'Xoá'))) return;`
    then `todos = todos.filter(t => !t.done)`, `commit()`, and show `clearedDone` unless `persist` returned `notSaved` (U1 — the
    failure message must win).
  - Count `n` from the **whole list**, not `visible()`/the filter, and re-count *after* the dialog closes (same reasoning as the
    `current` getter in the import handler, `app.js:105-108`: the list can change while the dialog is open).
  - `render()`: `#clear-done.hidden = todos.every(t => !t.done)` (U3: no button when nothing to clear).
  - Reuse: `commit()`, `persist()` via commit, `fill()`, `formatCount()`, `ask()`. No `innerHTML` with user text (S3); no
    dependency (S4).
- `tests/app.test.js` — `loadApp` gets an `answer` option (default `'no'`) so the fake dialog can say "Xoá"; record the yes-label too.

## Order of work
1. Write the tests below (they fail: no `#clear-done`). Person reviews.
2. `MESSAGES` + `index.html` button + `#confirm-yes`.
3. `ask()` label parameter; import still shows "Thay" (existing import tests stay green).
4. `clearDone()` + `render()` visibility.
5. `bash scripts/check.sh`; manual check in browser.

## Risks
- Irreversible, multi-item delete → S2 confirm; "Huỷ"/Esc must keep the list untouched and save nothing.
- Filter set to "Chưa xong": user cannot see what will be deleted → the question states the count.
- Changing `ask()` could break import's dialog → import tests cover it; default label keeps "Thay".
- Save fails (storage full): list on screen is cleared but not saved → must show `notSaved`, not the success line.
- Q1 unresolved = U2 conflict; don't ship before it is answered.

## Proof (tests in `tests/app.test.js`)
| Step | Test |
|---|---|
| 2,4 | 3 done + 2 open, answer "Huỷ": asked `Xoá 3 việc đã xong?…`, nothing saved, list unchanged |

I've written the plan to `<home>/.claude/plans/add-a-clear-completed-quirky-eagle.md`. I didn't change any project files.

**Size: Medium.** It touches four files: `app/index.html`, `app/app.js`, `app/backup.js` (new messages only) and `tests/app.test.js`.

**How it works:**
- **New button.** "Xoá việc đã xong" sits next to the task count. It's hidden when no task is finished.
- **Confirm first.** Clicking it asks `Xoá {n} việc đã xong? Không lấy lại được.` before anything is deleted. This is required by `policy-security#S2`, because the action deletes more than one task.
- **Count covers the whole list.** `n` counts every finished task, not just the ones the current filter shows. It's counted again after the dialog closes, the same way the import code handles a list that changes while it waits.
- **Reuses existing code:** `ask()`, `commit()`/`persist()`, `fill()`/`formatCount()`.
- **Failed save.** If saving fails, the "not saved" message (`MESSAGES.notSaved`) replaces the success message.
- **Dialog button label.** The dialog's yes button is hard-coded "Thay" (`app/index.html:37`), which is the wrong word for a delete. `ask()` gets a label parameter: import keeps "Thay" and clearing uses "Xoá".

**Decisions for you, Linh (UX) or Khoa (tech lead):**
1. **When only one task is finished, the policies conflict.** `policy-ux#U2` says single-item actions get no dialog and an Undo for 10 seconds instead, but the app has no Undo. I lean towards always confirming and writing that down as an exception to U2. Linh should make that call.
2. **Unreadable saved list:** I suggest showing the button anyway, the same as the other actions, since the banner already says changes won't be saved.
3. **Wording:** the proposed Vietnamese texts are in the plan and need Linh's approval.

**Process:** CLAUDE.md requires an accepted intent and spec before a plan, and none exists for this yet. The next step is `/write-intent`, unless the product owner waives it for a change this size. Either way, a person has to accept the plan before any code is written.

The plan also lists which test proves each step, plus manual keyboard checks.
